chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man travels during the month of Ramadan and departs after midday, he is obligated to fast that day and count it as part of Ramadan. If he enters a land before the emergence of dawn with the intention of staying there, he is obligated to fast that day. If he enters after the emergence of dawn, there is no fasting obligation upon him, and if he wishes, he may fast.
ai.seo_question: What are the fasting rules for a traveler who departs after midday or arrives in a new city during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'continuity of fast' (istimrar al-siyam) for travelers who depart after midday, requiring them to complete the day's fast even if they break it en route. It further clarifies the ruling upon arrival: if one intends to stay in a new location before dawn, the fast becomes obligatory; otherwise, it remains optional. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the traveler's intention (niyyah) and the specific timing of dawn as the decisive factor for obligation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man travels during a Month of Ramazan, so he goes out after half the day, so upon him is the Fast of that day, and he would be counted with it from a Month of Ramazan. So when he enters a land before the emergence of the dawn and he intends the staying with it, so upon him is the Fast of that day. So if he enters after the emergence of the dawn, so there are no Fasts upon him, and he so desires to, he can Fast’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man travels in the month of Ramadan and goes out after midday, he is required to fast that day and count it as that of the month of Ramadan. If he enters a place before dawn and wants to stay there (for ten days), he must fast that day, but if he enters after dawn, there he is not obligated for anything but he can fast if he wants.’”
